intended_object: The combinatorial n-th homotopy group π_n(X, x) of a simplicial set X at a vertex x (May, Ch. I §3–4): homotopy classes rel ∂Δ[n] of maps Δ[n] → X that send ∂Δ[n] to x. I took this from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The definition is Mathlib's `RelativeMorphism.HomotopyClass` applied to:
- the subcomplex `∂Δ[n]` of `Δ[n]`;
- the subcomplex of X generated by the vertex x;
- the constant map from `∂Δ[n]` onto that vertex.

A `RelativeMorphism` here is a map `Δ[n] ⟶ X` whose restriction to `∂Δ[n]` is constant at x, which is exactly a pointed n-simplex. Two of them are identified when there is a homotopy `Δ[n] ⊗ Δ[1] ⟶ X` that stays constant at x on `∂Δ[n] × Δ[1]`. This is the standard notion of homotopy relative to the boundary.

The quotient is taken by the equivalence relation generated by this relation. For a Kan complex the relation is already an equivalence relation, so the quotient is the usual combinatorial π_n. The docstring only promises a group structure for n ≥ 1 and Kan X, which is the right condition.

Degenerate case n = 0: `∂Δ[0]` is empty, so π 0 X x is the set of vertices modulo the equivalence relation generated by edges, i.e. π_0(X), with x as base point. This is correct.

Generality: the construction is stated for an arbitrary simplicial set and an arbitrary vertex, which is its natural setting. Mathlib at this commit has `PtSimplex`, `RelStruct` and `MulStruct`, but no homotopy-group type. That type is in the still-open PR #42435, which this definition follows. So there is no Mathlib counterpart to cite.
